testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What happens if brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Some brakes work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes fade faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: What are air brakes?

options.text: An effective way to stop large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effective way to stop large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: Know the maximum air loss allowed for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How does an S-cam brake create friction?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the outside of the drum.
The brake shoes press against the inside of the drum.
The brake shoes press against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when brake shoes press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment, especially if they overheat from heavy use. Check brake adjustment often.

questions.question: How do you remove water and compressor oil from an air storage tank?

options.text: Siphon the water and oil out.
Open the drain valve at the bottom of the tank.
The water and oil come out automatically when you use the brakes.
Use a sponge to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the drain valve at the bottom of the tank.
questions.explanation: Use the drain valve to remove water and oil from air storage tanks. If left in the tank, water and oil can damage the brakes. Manually operated tanks must be drained daily.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What should be done with water and compressor oil in an air brake system?

options.text: They are needed for the brakes to work.
Add more if levels are low.

questions.explanation: Compressed air systems naturally contain water and oil. If left to build up, they can damage the brakes. Open the drain valve on manually operated tanks every day to remove water and oil.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?
questions.explanation: An ABS helps the driver maintain control during hard braking, but it does not necessarily make the vehicle stop faster.

questions.question: Where is the ABS malfunction lamp on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle near the passenger door.

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have a yellow malfunction lamp on the instrument panel. Trailers have a yellow ABS lamp on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.
To stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are on every wheel of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What braking system does the brake pedal control?
questions.explanation: The service brake system works when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will speed up your vehicle on the downgrade.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: What does a tank endorsement allow you to transport?

options.text: It is optional for hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases, whether hazardous or not.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tanks completely.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve releases air?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, the system has a problem and needs to be checked by a mechanic.

questions.question: What color light indicates an ABS system problem?
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lights are usually yellow. Even if the ABS is not working, you will still have regular brakes.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake on a steep downgrade?

options.text: Ride the brakes all the way down.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this pattern all the way down the hill.
Use the brakes only near the bottom of the hill.
Apply steady pressure to the brake pedal all the way down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this pattern all the way down the hill.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downgrades, use brakes to help the engine slow you down. Apply the brakes until you feel the vehicle slow down, then release them. Once you drop about 5 mph below your safe speed, repeat the process.

questions.question: When the spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of the springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, you should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up so fuel reaches the engine.
Wait for air pressure to build in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving, let the compressor build air pressure to at least 100 psi in both brake systems.

questions.question: A front brake limiting valve usually has two markings. They read:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, the parking brake is applied by:
questions.explanation: In a newer vehicle with air brakes, the parking brake uses a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving:

options.text: You can brake only if there is enough air left in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before running out of air.
You can drive normally and check the brakes later.
You should stay at least 100 feet from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can brake only if there is enough air left in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. There may be a leak. You can only brake as long as there is enough air left in the tanks.
